question: What is the function of a diathermic wall in a thermodynamic system?

options.text: It allows the flow of only work.
It prevents the exchange of both matter and energy.
It allows the exchange of matter only.
It allows the flow of heat between systems.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It allows the flow of heat between systems.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A diathermic wall is a type of boundary in thermodynamics that **permits the transfer of heat** between two systems or between a system and its surroundings.
 
• It does not allow the exchange of matter between systems, ensuring that the systems remain physically separate.
 
• Diathermic walls are typically used in thermodynamic experiments to **study heat transfer** while isolating other forms of energy transfer, such as work.
 
• Heat transfer occurs because of the temperature difference between systems separated by a diathermic wall.
 
• The concept of diathermic walls is crucial in understanding **thermal equilibrium**, as heat flows until both systems reach the same temperature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Main Theme: Thermodynamic Walls**

 
 
• Thermodynamic walls are boundaries that separate systems and influence the type of interaction between them.
 
• They can be classified into different types, including **adiabatic walls** (prevent heat transfer), **diathermic walls** (allow heat transfer), and **rigid walls** (prevent work transfer).
 
• The study of these walls helps in understanding the exchange of energy in various thermodynamic processes.
